title: PrismML hopes its tiny LLM will change how we all use AI
slides: Can PrismML's tiny LLM replace giants?
It runs on phones, not data centers
But small models often hallucinate more quietly
Your next app might not need cloud at all
Test one offline task: does it hold up?
thread_text:
1. The quiet hallucination

A tiny model that runs on your phone might sound impressive, but it can invent facts without the loud warning signs of cloud giants.

2. No data center needed

PrismML's LLM runs locally on phones, cutting out server costs and latency. But that convenience hides a trade-off.

3. Offline, but less reliable

Small models hallucinate more quietly because they lack the massive context windows of their larger cousins. You might not notice the error until it's too late.

4. Your app, your rules

Offline AI means no cloud dependency, but also no safety net. If the model fails, there's no fallback to a bigger server.

5. Test it on one task

Pick a simple offline task—like summarizing a note—and see if PrismML's model holds up. Does it save you time or create more editing?

instagram.caption:
A language model that lives on your phone, not in a data center.

PrismML built a tiny LLM that runs locally, skipping server costs and latency. 📱

The catch: small models hallucinate more quietly. They lack the big context windows, so errors slip past you until it's too late. ⚠️

Offline AI means no cloud dependency, but also no fallback if it fails.

For content work, that changes your editing: you can't assume the draft is safe. 🧠

Pick one task—summarizing a note—and check if it saves time or adds cleanup. Would you trust it on a deadline? 🤔
